A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConFu research work. Text, equations, figures and tables are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendices A–B in v2; v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 report original SpecBench measurements and component ablations using Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.

after.justification: v2 retains the Llama experiments and adds original Qwen3-4B results, GPU-memory measurements and training-length ablations in Tables 3, 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same contemplate tokens, soft prompts, MoE components, inference procedure, anchor sampling and prediction replication. The new experiments do not introduce a method modification.

E1.justification: The reported training datasets remain ShareGPT and UltraChat-200K, and evaluation retains the same SpecBench tasks. Adding Qwen3-4B and varying training length changes model configurations and experimental settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: EAGLE-3 remains the evaluated external comparator, including in the new Qwen comparison. The original component-ablation comparisons are preserved in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen3-4B evaluation using the existing temperature and draft-node grid, tests training lengths 4 and 10 alongside the default 7, and measures peak GPU memory with 60 nodes over 10 SpecBench samples. These extend the evaluation without revising the existing Llama protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a focused sensitivity study of draft-training length, while Appendix A measures memory overhead relative to EAGLE-3. The original MoE and prediction-replication ablations are unchanged, merely renumbered as Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging the new memory measurements over 10 SpecBench samples specifies an evaluation sample size, not repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands the results with Qwen3-4B performance, memory measurements and training-length comparisons. In new Table 3, at 60 nodes and temperature 0, ConFu versus EAGLE-3 achieves accepted length 4.60 versus 3.81 and speed-up ratio 3.20 versus 2.69. Existing Table 1 also revises ten per-task acceptance-length values for ConFu at 30 nodes and temperature 0.7, including RP 3.82 to 3.99 and SUMM 3.88 to 3.82, without a stated setting change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and training objectives, including Equations 1–3, are unchanged. v2 adds no formal assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the quantitative performance claim from 8–11% improvements on Llama 3B/8B to also approximately 20% on Qwen3-4B. The central methodological contributions and novelty claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 newly concludes that ConFu is robust to the tested training lengths and incurs minimal memory overhead, citing Tables 6 and 5. Existing explanations involving future guidance and error accumulation, and the caveat about computation growing with draft-node count, are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly discloses the default training length of 7; this does not establish a changed default. The additions specify alternative lengths and the memory-measurement sample size, while existing hardware and baseline-access information remain unchanged. Qwen-specific training and checkpoint details are not supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography and positioning relative to EAGLE, BiTA, pause tokens and latent reasoning are unchanged after accounting for table relocation and pagination.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the abstract and experimental discussion, with new experiment paragraphs and appendix headings. Section 4.1 corrects the swapped Llama version labels. The introduction, methodology, related-work discussion and conclusion retain their narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Qwen comparison as Table 3 and the memory and training-length displays as appendix Tables 5–6. The original ablation table moves and becomes Table 4, with consequent text reflow. Figures 1–4 and the established display style remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Qwen3-4B comparison adds evidence that ConFu's benefits extend beyond Llama, while Tables 5–6 provide concrete checks of memory cost and training-length sensitivity that v1 lacked. These strengthen empirical support and practical assessment. The gains remain limited by sparse Qwen-specific setup information and the absence of uncertainty estimates.
